evals.prompt: Rewrite the AGENTS.md in this repo so it's tight and follows Anthropic's guidance.
evals.expected_output: AGENTS.md rewritten under 60 lines with personas and default-behaviour rules cut, generic tool wording replaced by the pyproject commands, the stale mypy command flagged, and a grouped report of cuts with follow-ups.
expectations: A1: The rewritten AGENTS.md is under 60 lines.

A2 [R]: No persona text ('You are a senior Python engineer', 'act like one') and no default-behaviour rule ('think step by step', 'read the relevant files before editing', 'match the existing code style') remains.
A3 [R]: 'the formatter', 'the linter' and 'the tests' are replaced by `uv run ruff format .`, `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run pytest`.
A4: The Conventional Commits rule is kept.
A5 [R][D]: The report lists the cuts grouped by kind (persona, default behaviour, linter-enforced, decision tree, emphasis), each group with a reason.

A6 [D]: The rewrite adds no rule that contradicts .claude/rules/testing.md (for example it doesn't keep or add 'unittest.TestCase'), and the report lists `/doctor prompt-audit` as the follow-up for cross-file contradictions or includes its findings.
A7 [R][D]: `uv run mypy src` is flagged as not defined by pyproject.toml or removed, and no command absent from pyproject.toml is introduced.
A8 [D]: The report lists `/doctor` as the follow-up for trimming and relocation (Claude Code) or lists relocation candidates (elsewhere), and no new files are created.
A9: No git commit was made.

evals.expected_output: rewritten-AGENTS.md contains every preference once, specialized to the project ('main', the ruff format command), with a report that accounts for every input rule.
expectations: Every preference from coding-preferences.md is present exactly once in the result.
[D] 'the default branch' is rendered as `main` and 'the formatter' as `uv run ruff format .`.
The result has no duplicate lines (for example only one 'tests with every change' rule and one type-hints rule).
[D] The report accounts for every input rule as kept, combined or dropped as a duplicate or conflict.

evals.prompt: Merge team-preferences.md into AGENTS.md. AGENTS.md takes precedence.
evals.expected_output: The squash-merge rule from AGENTS.md wins over 'never squash'; the other team preferences are merged; the conflict is listed.
expectations: The merged file keeps 'squash-merge pull requests' and doesn't contain 'never squash'.
`go vet ./...` and table-driven tests are kept.
[D] The report lists the squash-versus-merge-commit conflict and which side won.
[D] team-preferences.md is neither deleted nor modified; only AGENTS.md changes.

evals.prompt: This repo has both an AGENTS.md and a CLAUDE.md that overlap. Merge them.
evals.expected_output: A canonical AGENTS.md holding the shared rules and a CLAUDE.md that starts with @AGENTS.md and holds only the Claude-specific lines.
expectations: [D] CLAUDE.md starts with `@AGENTS.md`.
[D] CLAUDE.md holds only Claude-specific lines (plan mode for src/billing/, subagent for integration tests) and no rule already in AGENTS.md.
AGENTS.md keeps the shared commands and rules once each.
The report accounts for every input rule and mentions the `claude-md-and-agents-md` setting as the alternative.

[D] The report flags 'TypeScript strict mode; no `any`' (AGENTS.md) vs 'avoid `any`' (CLAUDE.md) as a refinement or conflict rather than a plain duplicate, and the result keeps the stricter 'no `any`'.

evals.expected_output: AGENTS.md (the symlink target) is rewritten; CLAUDE.md is still a symlink to it.
expectations: [D] AGENTS.md is edited (persona and 'read files before you edit them' are gone).
[D] CLAUDE.md is still a symlink pointing to AGENTS.md.
'the linter' becomes `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`.

evals.prompt: Rewrite this skill so it follows the official skill authoring guidance.
evals.expected_output: Third-person description keeping every trigger context; CSV explainer cut; workflow and example kept; references flattened; the dated line under Old patterns; validation passes.
expectations: The description is in third person and still mentions bad headers, duplicate rows, mixed date formats and tidy/normalize/dedupe requests.
The 'What is a CSV file?' and 'Why cleaning matters' explanations are cut; the workflow steps and the header example are kept.
details.md is linked from SKILL.md (or merged), and advanced.md no longer links to another reference file.
The 'As of March 2025' line is under an 'Old patterns' heading or reworded without a date, and skill-creator's `quick_validate.py` and the repo's `tools/lint_skill.py` both exit 0 on the result.
The SKILL.md body is not padded toward 1,000-3,000 words and stays under 500 lines.
No reference content is lost: the `--dayfirst` and `--keep-duplicates` options and the list of supported date formats still appear somewhere in the skill (moved or merged is fine).

evals.prompt: Run evals on my pdf skill.
evals.expected_output: Routed to skill-creator in one line; no file changed.
expectations: The response routes the request to skill-creator.
No file is created or changed by this skill.

evals.prompt: Audit my CLAUDE.md, don't change anything.
evals.expected_output: Routed to /doctor prompt-audit (run or suggested); claude-md-improver not invoked; no file changed.
expectations: The response runs or suggests `/doctor prompt-audit` on CLAUDE.md (outside Claude Code: report-only findings).
claude-md-improver is not invoked.
CLAUDE.md is unchanged.

evals.prompt: My CLAUDE.md is too long, cut whatever Claude can figure out from the code.
evals.expected_output: Tells the user /doctor does this; no rewrite; no file changed.
expectations: The response says `/doctor` trims content derivable from the code.
No rewrite runs and CLAUDE.md is unchanged.

evals.expected_output: Points to claude-md-improver or /revise-claude-md when installed, otherwise says this skill doesn't add content; no file changed.
expectations: The response points to `claude-md-improver` or `/revise-claude-md`, or says this skill doesn't add content.
CLAUDE.md is unchanged.
